assembly_checklist: Pick the genre/era anchor and mood sentence first; keep the brief prioritized in skeleton order.
Write the vocal as a full personality sentence (timbre + delivery + attitude), not adjectives.
Use rhythm-feel language for pace; set the BPM field for the record and expect ~152.
For a keeper attempt, append the timestamped arrangement script with an intensity curve; script the edges and plan to check the first/last 10 seconds.
Close with one production sentence + one exclusion sentence — and hold zero expectation that they move the master.
Reuse the song's seed across variants; download WAV + stems; loudness-match listening copies before judging.
Plan the finish at brief time: stems -> Ableton (sub discipline, presence lift, loudness). Prompting will not do this part.

blocks.effect_note: The exact Exp B revision instruction. Result: +1.3 dB loudness by meter, 'sounds better' by the user's ear, no measured change in band balance. This is the strongest single revision turn we have on record.
blocks.text: Tighten the low end and reduce sub boom; keep the bass notes short and punchy. Make the vocal drier, closer and further upfront, with brighter, crisper presence. Lift the overall brightness and loudness of the master. Change nothing else — same lyrics, structure, tempo and melody.

blocks.text: Standing instructions candidate: 'Default to a tight, disciplined low end, a dry upfront lead vocal, and a bright, loud master unless a brief says otherwise.'

brief_skeleton: A [length] [genre + era anchor] track. [Mood/energy sentence.] Built on [lead texture/instrument], [rhythm element], and [accent sounds]. Drums: [drum character]. [Tempo/rhythm-feel sentence.] Lead vocal: [vocal personality sentence]. Sing the lyrics in the Lyrics field verbatim, in order. [Structure sentence or timestamped arrangement script.] Production: [production sentence]. No [exclusion list].

evidence_grades.community: Third-party guides/reviews only; not yet verified by us.
evidence_grades.measured: Verified on our own analyzed takes (analyzer + section pass + vocal profile) or the user's ear, 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-29.
evidence_grades.official: Stated in Google's official Lyria prompt guide or Flow support docs.
evidence_grades.official+measured: Documented by Google AND exercised in our runs; the effect note says what actually happened.
evidence_grades.untested: Sourced but never run by us. Treat as a hypothesis with a price tag (~5 credits).

known_ceilings.detail: Every Flow take measured exactly 152.0 BPM, zero drift, against a 158 ask delivered three different ways. Suno's take, by contrast, measured 143.6 against its 145 ask.

Sub-bass share 66.8-75.6% and presence 3.8-4.9% on every Flow take, across brief prose, Compose fields, a global remix and a timestamped arrangement. The Suno take: 53.9% sub, 7.0% presence. Finishing in Ableton (or stem-level repair) is mandatory, not optional.
F minor was requested on three Flow runs and never landed (outcomes: ~D#, G minor/D major pair, D major). Do not write briefs that depend on an exact key from Lyria.

Flow RMS fell across the series (-16.9 -> -19.5 -> -18.2 -> -19.6 dBFS) while peaks stayed near 0 dBFS: the takes are dynamic, not clipped-quiet. Loudness-match (-14 LUFS) before any A/B judgment — louder reads as better, and the user confirmed the effect on E1.

Arrangement scripting moved macro-dynamics (19.9 dB range, script-shaped section curve). A Producer revision moved loudness (+1.3 dB) and, per the user's ear, overall quality. Vocal personality prose reliably lands the requested voice family. Everything else about the master has, so far, been immovable by prompting.

model: Lyria 3.5 — flagship entry in the Flow Music Compose model menu (verified live 2026-10-29). Per user ruling 2026-10-29: Lyria 3 Pro (legacy menu entry) is outdated and never used; this library targets 3.5 until Lyria 4.0 ships.
name: Lyria 3.5 Brief Library
principle: Lyria does not eat Suno-style comma tag stacks. It eats a coherent, prioritized prose brief (Google's official Lyria prompt guide). This library is therefore prose building blocks, not tags: each block is a sentence or phrase that drops into one slot of the brief skeleton, graded by evidence so future briefs stop re-deriving lessons we already paid for.
skeleton_order_source: Official guide order (genre/style, mood, instrumentation, tempo/rhythm, vocal style) + our Compose practice: lyrics live in the dedicated Lyrics field, never inside the brief.
sources: Google Cloud official Lyria prompt guide (updated 2026-10-28): brief structure, detailed-structure timestamp workflow with per-segment key/BPM/Intensity, negative_prompt parameter.
Google Flow support docs: Producer personalization (Instructions, Memories, custom Flows), Producer/Ghostwriter tiers.
Our measured runs: Sep 21 2026 Flow mapping + takes; Oct 29 2026 one-shot, Exp A, Exp B, E1 — analyzer/section/vocal-profile outputs in ~/workspace/audio-analysis/output/ and flow-compare/.
User ear verdicts, Oct 29 2026: Exp B 'sounds better'; E1 singer improved, raw render too quiet, -14 LUFS copy 'noticeably louder'.
